forces.title: Systemic supply chain volatility and disruptions impacting global trade
forces.description: Risks have evolved from isolated events to systemic, multi-tier, interconnected, and persistent volatility, driven by geopolitical situations, environmental factors, and cyber threats. These disruptions are costing companies an estimated USD 12 billion annually, keeping supply chains constantly on edge and demanding proactive strategies from logistics and freight operators.

forces.title: Global supply chains redesigning for resilience over pure cost efficiency
forces.description: Traditionally designed for efficiency, global supply chains now face geopolitical instability, tariffs, and export limitations. This has exposed weaknesses like concentrated production and heavy reliance on inter-continental transport. Trade is now prioritizing resilience, leading to restructuring into regional clusters with trusted partnerships and geographic diversification, significantly impacting global logistics flows.

forces.title: Rising operating costs and inflationary pressures challenge profitability
forces.description: The infrastructure and transport sector faces significant threats from rising costs and inflationary pressures (79% of CEOs), which increase project expenses, cause delays, and depress margins. Parcel logistics also sees persistent cost increases from rising fuel and labor expenses, making cost reduction a top challenge for 9 out of 10 shippers and carriers due to their impact on operational profitability.

forces.title: AI and digitalization driving logistics optimization and operational efficiency
forces.description: AI-powered predictive maintenance, logistics optimization, and digital twins enhance efficiency, safety, and asset performance across transport systems. In smart logistics, AI and machine learning improve demand forecasting, reroute shipments, manage warehouse flows, and optimize routing/load planning, leading to significant cost reductions, improved truck utilization, and a shift from reactive to proactive operations.

forces.title: Shippers increasingly expect AI-enabled logistics and digital partnerships
forces.description: Over 40% of shippers now expect Logistics Service Providers (LSPs) to offer AI-enabled logistics, viewing it as a new baseline for service, alongside real-time tracking APIs, performance dashboards, and flexible options. Integrating technology is seen as the biggest hurdle to changing carriers, indicating that advanced digital capabilities are becoming crucial for retaining strategic relationships and competitive differentiation.

forces.title: Unclear AI ROI and internal capability gaps impede widespread adoption
forces.description: Despite AI's transformative potential, approximately 40% of LSPs and shippers cite unclear return on investment and internal capability gaps as the primary barriers to adoption, more so than cost or technical complexity. This signifies that AI success is largely an operating model challenge, requiring significant workforce reskilling, integration into existing systems, and a clear articulation of value to drive broader implementation.

forces.title: Modernizing and digitizing global supply chains and logistics networks
forces.description: The infrastructure and transport sector is actively engaged in modernizing and digitizing global supply chains and logistics networks. This initiative aims to enhance the movement, tracking, and storage of goods, driven by a global shift towards digitally-driven economies and the pressing need for greater efficiency, transparency, and agility across increasingly complex logistical operations worldwide.

forces.title: Government policy and investment fostering integrated logistics infrastructure in India
forces.description: India's government is strategically investing ₹12.2 lakh crore in infrastructure, focusing on dedicated freight corridors, new waterways, and a Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme to optimize logistics costs and increase multimodal share. Technology-led customs reforms, GST cuts on freight, and incentives for rail-anchored logistics parks further streamline operations and reduce friction, supporting a nationally integrated, technology-enabled freight grid.

forces.title: Shippers adopting multicarrier models and selective logistics insourcing
forces.description: Over half of parcel shippers have redesigned their network strategy post-pandemic, shifting towards multicarrier models to enhance resilience, reduce lock-in, and align costs with service. Retailers are also selectively insourcing logistics, particularly in dense urban areas, impacting carrier volumes and increasing competition for Freight, Logistics & Supply Chain providers by internalizing critical value chain segments.

forces.title: Policy focus and investment to strengthen India's cold chains and modern warehouses
forces.description: India's Budget 2026-27 is expected to accelerate investment in agricultural infrastructure for post-harvest management, including cold chains, modern warehouses, processing units, and digital supply-chain management. This aims to address significant losses (15-20% for perishables) due to inadequate storage and logistics, fostering resilience and efficiency in the food supply chain and creating opportunities for specialized logistics providers.

forces.title: Increased freight forwarding costs due to global supply chain disruptions
forces.description: From 2019 to 2021, freight forwarding costs increased by 11.6% annually, primarily due to pandemic-related disruptions to global supply chains, including travel restrictions, quarantining, and testing. This rise contributed significantly to the overall increase in operating expenses for shipping companies, highlighting a direct and cyclical cost pressure on the freight and logistics sector.

forces.title: Complexity of decarbonizing supply chains poses significant obstacle
forces.description: Decarbonizing supply chains is identified as the number one obstacle to achieving net-zero goals for infrastructure and transport CEOs (32%). This complexity is a major concern, as supply chain emissions often constitute the largest carbon footprint of major projects, requiring significant effort and industry-wide involvement, supported by government, to develop and implement effective sustainable logistics solutions.

viewpoints.title: AI progress critical for logistics competitiveness, driving market confidence and differentiation
viewpoints.description: AI has become a top agenda item in logistics, with capital markets increasingly viewing AI progress as a signal of future competitiveness. The logistics industry is now in an AI execution phase, where scaling AI into daily workflows will determine competitive advantage and widen the gap between adopters and non-adopters, compelling LSPs to move faster to meet shipper demand.

viewpoints.title: Future of logistics to be defined by scaled AI and intelligence, not just infrastructure
viewpoints.description: As supply chains grow more complex, their future will be shaped by intelligence and effective AI deployment, not solely by physical infrastructure. Companies that successfully scale AI will be the ones building resilient supply chains, indicating a fundamental shift in competitive advantage towards those who can consistently integrate AI into their core operations and decision-making processes.

viewpoints.title: CEOs prioritize supply chain resilience amidst decarbonization complexity and global uncertainty
viewpoints.description: Infrastructure and transport CEOs identify supply chain resilience as the biggest influence on short-term decisions (33%), highlighting vulnerability to global uncertainty. Decarbonizing supply chains also presents the number one obstacle to achieving net-zero goals (32%), signifying significant environmental and operational challenges for the sector. Fractured, unstandardized supply chains add to costs.

viewpoints.title: Infrastructure and transport sector CEOs optimistic about growth and digitization
viewpoints.description: 84% of CEOs express confidence in the infrastructure and transport sector's growth, with 87% confident in their own organizations, highest among all industries surveyed. This optimism is driven by the pivotal role of infrastructure and transport in digitally-driven economies, including modernizing global supply chains and logistics networks for movement, tracking, and storage of goods.

viewpoints.title: AI crucial for proactive navigation of systemic supply chain volatility and intelligent logistics
viewpoints.description: Supply chains face systemic, multi-tier, and persistent volatility, costing companies an estimated USD 12 billion annually. AI is moving to the core of operations, enabling predictive analytics to anticipate disruptions, digital twins to simulate networks, and AI agents to automate decisions, transforming logistics from reactive to intelligent for enhanced resilience and efficiency.

viewpoints.title: India poised to rebalance freight modal mix with rail and multimodal logistics
viewpoints.description: India has a significant opportunity to shift freight from roads (70% share) to rail (25%), leveraging rail's lower cost (INR1.9 vs INR3.78 per tonne-km). Dedicated freight corridors, Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals, and the Unified Logistics Interface Platform are driving record rail volumes and substantial private investment, signaling real potential for rebalancing the national freight landscape.

viewpoints.title: India's fragmented supply chain requires ecosystem-wide AI adoption for efficiency
viewpoints.description: India's supply chains, characterized by fragmentation, varied digitalization, and infrastructure gaps, stand to benefit significantly from ecosystem-wide AI adoption. Policy support through PM Gati Shakti, ULIP, National Logistics Policy, and the IndiaAI Mission is crucial to strengthen digital infrastructure, integrate data, and foster deep-tech logistics AI solutions, unlocking substantial savings and creating predictive logistics corridors.

viewpoints.title: Logistics LSPs lag in AI adoption despite growing shipper expectations and clear value
viewpoints.description: While over 40% of shippers increasingly expect AI-enabled logistics, only 40% of LSPs deploy AI beyond pilots, and just one in ten embed it into core operations, with only 13% reporting measurable value. LSPs must accelerate AI deployment, especially given that productivity gains, cost reduction, and efficiency are primary drivers, but unclear ROI and internal capability gaps remain major barriers.

viewpoints.title: Parcel logistics must shift to cost intelligence amid e-commerce-driven structural changes
viewpoints.description: Parcel logistics faces slowing growth, rising costs, and inefficiencies from underused assets and fragmented e-commerce volumes, particularly in last-mile delivery (50-60% of total cost). The industry needs to transition from cost cutting to 'cost intelligence,' building networks centered on Out-of-Home delivery, integrated returns, flexible ecosystems, and leveraging automation and AI for productivity and dynamic pricing to overcome these structural challenges.

viewpoints.title: Intelligent order management, with AI/automation, is essential for consumer goods supply chains
viewpoints.description: Intelligent order management, powered by AI and automation, is pivotal for consumer goods organizations to transition from reactive to real-time, data-driven supply chain execution. It significantly lowers logistics and operational costs, improves availability (e.g., 10-15% incremental sales on B-class SKUs), and builds competitive, future-ready, omnichannel-responsive supply chains by optimizing routing and load planning.

demand_drivers.description: GCTs facilitate seamless transfer between different transport modes, driven by government policy and private investment, increasing demand for integrated freight services.

pnl_drivers.description: Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) and GCTs enable faster, more reliable, and cost-effective rail movement, attracting more freight volumes and enhancing revenue for associated logistics services.

market_sizing.methodology: Freight revenues generated from Gati Shakti Multi‑Modal Cargo Terminals (GCTs) in India.

demand_drivers.description: Consistent, ecosystem-wide AI deployment across Indian ports, trucking, warehousing, and multimodal operations is expected to drive substantial efficiency gains and cost reductions.

pnl_drivers.description: AI-driven systems, digital twins, and predictive modeling optimize port operations, eliminating unnecessary container moves and improving truck turnaround times, leading to significant cost savings.
AI's application across the entire port logistics ecosystem leads to overall operational efficiencies and substantial annual cost reductions beyond just cargo handling.

new_opportunities.description: Consistent AI deployment could save nearly INR20,000 crore annually in cargo handling at Indian ports.
Consistent AI deployment could save another INR15,000 crore annually in broader port logistics operations.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated potential annual savings from consistent AI deployment across major ports and corridors in India.

demand_drivers.description: The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme, operationalizing new waterways, and increased budget outlay for infrastructure are driving the shift to water-based logistics modes.

pnl_drivers.description: Shifting freight to more cost-effective modes like waterways is expected to reduce overall logistics expenses, improving profitability for businesses and enhancing India's trade competitiveness.

new_opportunities.description: Policy initiatives aim to double the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping from 6% to 12% by 2047, offering significant growth opportunities for operators and infrastructure providers in these segments.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Inland waterways and coastal shipping growth

market_sizing.methodology: Government target to increase the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping in India's overall logistics modal mix by 2047.
